subject: PrecisionCare RFP: PHI controls, data residency & BAA next steps

Subject: PrecisionCare RFP: Security controls & PHI handling - initial Qs

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is a workbook of targeted technical questions (PrecisionCare_RFP_Security_Questions_v1.xlsx). A few high-level items we need clarified before moving to procurement: 

- Can Redwood’s hosted API be configured to never persist full request payloads that contain PHI? We need confirmation of retention windows and scrub/TTL options.
- What is the process for a BAA? We typically require a two-week turnaround and have a few redlines around data access and audit logs.
- Do you support regional data residency for patient data (specifically US-only storage) and can you provide infrastructure details?
- We also want to validate control mappings to our security questionnaire (SOC2 + specific PHI controls).

Can we get an initial response this week? We’re scheduling a short security Q&A next Tuesday.

Regards,
Sarah Kim
Security Program Manager
PrecisionCare Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for the detailed workbook. Looping in Rishi (Head of Security) and Laura (Legal) to cover technical and contract items. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with a short packet and a draft BAA for your redlines.

1) Retention and PHI in hosted API:
- Redwood’s hosted API can be configured per-customer to disable persistent request logging for full payloads that are marked PHI. We provide a customer-facing toggle in Console plus API flags. Default is to keep minimal telemetry for 7 days; for production PHI workloads we support 0-90 day retention windows depending on plan and agreement.

2) BAA process & timeline:
- We have a standard BAA template and typically turn around a signed agreement within 10 business days after scope confirmation. Laura will attach a draft BAA for review. If PrecisionCare needs specific redlines we can escalate to our GC.

3) Data residency:
- Hosted (US) region: Redwood operates isolated data pods in us-west-2 and us-east-1. Customers can opt into US-only storage and compute for PHI; we document the exact services and storage endpoints in the technical packet.

4) Control mappings / evidence: 
- We can provide SOC2 Type II report (redacted), control matrix mapping to HIPAA/PHI items, and evidence packages on request. Rishi: can you confirm log/audit retention and access control notes?

Next steps: we’ll send a short technical packet + draft BAA by Monday and can join your security Q&A on Tue (please propose a time).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales – Healthcare
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrecisionCare RFP: Security controls & PHI handling - initial Qs

Hi Sarah,

A few technical clarifications to complement Neha’s note — I'm including concrete control/evidence we can provide: 

- Request logging: For PHI-scoped endpoints we support a no-persist mode where raw request bodies are not written to long-term object storage. Short-term in-memory buffers are used for inference and evicted immediately; you can require no disk persistence in the account config.

- Audit logs & access: All operator/admin actions are audited and immutable for the agreed retention period. We can forward timestamped audit bundles and support on-demand log extracts for audits.

- Encryption & keys: Data in transit is TLS1.3; data at rest is AES-256. Customers can use customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for model artifacts and stored artifacts.

- Model serving: PHI must be explicitly labeled at the request header level to trigger PHI handling workflows (prefix header: X-Redwood-PHI: true). We’ll document header usage in the packet.

Attachments I will share: redacted SOC2-TypeII-Report-2025.pdf and a control mapping spreadsheet. Laura will follow up on BAA language around subprocessor lists.

-Rishi
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Procurement team,

Attached is our standard BAA (Redwood_DRAFT_BAA_20260620.docx). Key callouts: 
- Scope: covers Hosted API, Dedicated pools (if elected), and Console access for the duration of the contract.
- Subprocessors: we list major cloud providers and inference partners; we accept a mutual notification obligation for changes and can provide a subprocessor dataflow diagram on request.
- Audit & access: we accept reasonable audit requests and can provide SOC2 artifacts under NDA.
- Data return/destruction: on termination we will purge customer PHI from active storage within 30 days and from backups within 90 days unless otherwise agreed.

Proposed review workflow to hit your two-week target: 
1) PrecisionCare marks redlines in the attached doc and returns by EOD Tue (23 Jun).
2) Laura + GC review and provide consolidated comments within 3 business days.
3) If material redlines are proposed, we’ll escalate to an exec call to resolve remaining open items.

I’ve included links to the technical packet and SOC2 in our shared folder for your team. If that timeline works I can send a DocuSign when we have a mutually-agreed version.

Regards,
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference
